claims.text: Increasing lattice distortion at FCC/BCC interfaces enhances dislocation pinning.
Enhanced dislocation pinning at FCC/BCC interfaces reduces creep deformation during continuous loading.
The starting coating is an as-deposited FCC/BCC high-entropy alloy with moderate lattice distortion and standard coherency at its phase boundaries.
Increasing substrate temperature or altering sputtering power can selectively increase lattice distortion at FCC/BCC interfaces.
The proposed deposition or compositional modifications can reduce interfacial coherency at FCC/BCC boundaries.
The degree of lattice distortion and interfacial coherency at FCC/BCC or FCC/B2 boundaries governs the proposed response.
Increasing lattice distortion hinders dislocation motion during sustained stress.
Hindering dislocation motion delays progressive plastic deformation relative to the baseline coating.
Coatings with greater interfacial lattice distortion will have a lower creep rate than the standard as-deposited coating.
Coatings with greater interfacial lattice distortion will show reduced dislocation mobility.
Coatings with greater interfacial lattice distortion will show a delayed onset of tertiary creep.
The proposed effect operates under moderate-to-high temperatures and sustained loads where creep is significant.
The proposed effect is expected to persist only while stress and temperature do not induce phase transformations or severe microstructural instability.
Outside the stated stability regime, mechanisms other than interfacial lattice-distortion pinning may dominate creep.
Grain size and incidental precipitates may also affect creep behavior.
High-resolution TEM can assess interfacial lattice distortion and dislocation arrangements relevant to the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The intervention proposes minor compositional tweaks while also requiring the overall composition to remain constant. A composition-changing intervention cannot literally preserve the same overall composition unless the intended constraint is defined more narrowly.
